instructions: Fill a large pot with water and 1 tbsp of the salt. Put it over high heat.
Finely chop the onion, the bell pepper and the carrots into pieces about the size of a pea. Mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, pepper, carrots and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Add the garlic and oregano. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell the garlic.
Add the crushed tomatoes. Bring to a bubble, lower the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
While the sauce simmers, add the macaroni to the boiling water and cook until it's tender, following the package time. Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Stir the sugar, the pepper and the last 1/2 tsp salt into the sauce. Add the macaroni and toss for 1 minute, adding a splash of the pasta water if it's thick.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve in bowls with the sauce spooned over.
method_notes: The sources agree on macaroni in a slow-cooked tomato sofrito of onion and garlic. Directo al Paladar's grandmother version simmers fresh tomato for an hour and balances the acid with a teaspoon of sugar; the University Pablo de Olavide version adds carrot and pepper and takes 30 minutes, and that quicker build is followed here, with canned crushed tomato instead of fried tomato. The sugar and the pasta water are kept from the first source. Heat and cheese are left out so it stays mild.
